channel.title: The Wilson Times - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from The Wilson Times (wilsontimes.com)

item.title: Swing voters aren’t necessarily ticket-splitters
item.description: In North Carolina’s 2026 midterms, base voters, swing voters and shrinking ranks of ticket-splitters will shape key races, as John Hood explains using recent statewide election results.

item.title: Groundhog Day governing: Why NC can’t move forward while stuck in this tax loop
item.description: North Carolina’s yearly income tax cuts chiefly aid the wealthy and corporations, weakening schools, child care and services. The author says 2026 must finally break this loop.

item.title: Our Opinion: Don’t be snowed by net-erologists’ phony forecasts
item.description: North Carolina TV meteorologists push back on “net-erologists” whose hyped snow forecasts fuel confusion and abuse, urging viewers to trust trained experts and keep criticism civil.

item.title: Investors become scapegoat for housing crisis
item.description: A North Carolina critic says professional landlords are scapegoated for the housing crisis, though they make up just 2% of investor buys, diverting attention from interest rates and construction costs.

item.title: Pittman should show his work on Johnson & Johnson project
item.description: Letter urges Rep. Dante Pittman to detail his role, meetings and records in securing Johnson & Johnson's second Wilson plant, contrasting his vague column with Sen. Buck Newton's account.

item.title: Lawfare doesn’t inspire confidence in sheriff race
item.description: Former N.C. Rep. Ken Fontenot recalls his own party registration glitch to argue that using technicalities against Republican sheriff candidate Knight is unfair “lawfare” that undermines confidence in local elections.

item.title: Barton women let 24-point lead slip away in 78-75 loss to UNC Pembroke
item.description: Barton women squander a 24-point lead as UNC Pembroke surges back with a 28-10 fourth quarter to win 78-75, led by Bre’Asia Washington’s 31 points and a decisive edge at the free-throw line.

item.title: Our schools, our children await outcome of Leandro case
item.description: A Wilson County school board member, writing as a parent and lawyer, urges the N.C. Supreme Court to end decades of delay in the Leandro school funding case and uphold students’ constitutional rights.

item.title: Second-half surge lifts UNC Pembroke past Bulldogs 85-70
item.description: UNC Pembroke used a dominant second half and 42 free throws to pull away from Barton 85-70, snapping the Bulldogs’ three-game win streak despite four players scoring in double figures at Wilson Gymnasium.

item.title: Area Calendar, Jan. 30-31, 2026
item.description: Barton College launches its spring sports season Friday, Jan. 30, with softball, men's lacrosse and men's tennis in action along with men's and women's basketball while Southern Nash visits Fike for a high school hoops tripleheader.
